content.thinking:
I need to write the whole file in one pass, planning out imports from three, the builder helper, rng math, and pixel paint utilities. The default export should be a parameterless function returning a THREE.Object3D, built via createBuilder with a name like "monsterTruck" and returning its root.

For realistic proportions I'm sizing tires at 1.6m diameter with 0.9m width, overall height around 3.4m, width 3.6m, length 5.5m, and a 3.0m wheelbase, with axles sitting at 0.85m so the tires just touch the ground. I'm working out how to build wheels as cylinders rotated to align their axis along X, then painting the tires with cellPaint and adding tread lugs as small boxes spaced around the circumference using rotation math to orient each lug radially.

Still writing tire geometry...

Now I'm laying out the wheel hub assembly with rim, beadlock bolts, hub cap, and lug nuts, then positioning the axles and differential pumpkin between the wheel centers, and setting the wheelbase with front and rear axle positions.

For suspension, I'm adding coilovers running from each axle up to the chassis mount points, plus yellow spring rods with rings and link bars connecting axle to chassis. Then I'm framing the chassis rails and cross members as box shapes running the length of the frame, and starting to block out the truck body with lower bed/hood panels above the frame.

Now I'm considering building the body as an extruded side-profile silhouette instead of separate boxes—defining a 2D outline along the z-axis with the cab, hood, and bed contours, then extruding it with thickness along x so the walls get a chamfered edge, possibly adding flame decals via position-based cell painting.

Working out flame paint logic...

Now I want dark glass cab windows inset slightly on the sides plus a slanted windshield, extruded thin along the cab profile with a pixel-art sky reflection texture. I'm sketching the cab body outline as a series of (z,y) points starting from the low hood front.

Still plotting the outline coordinates, continuing to the rear bed and tail, and I need to account for the wheel arches sitting above the 1.7m diameter tyres.

I'm extruding the body shape along the x-axis with a thickness around 1.9 units, keeping bevels subtle for a blocky pixel-art style. Now I'm adding hood details—a blower scoop with chrome stacks on top, plus a front grille positioned on the slanted face using small decal boxes.

Still placing front-end details: a textured grille box, glowing headlight boxes on either side, chrome bumpers front and rear, a bull bar tube, and a roof-mounted lightbar with six glowing lamps.

Now I'm adding exhaust stacks as angled silver pipes behind the cab, a door number decal rendered via pixel art on a white disc, small pixel-art panel line details and handles on the doors, and side mirrors as simple boxes—then moving on to bed details like rollbar hoops.

For the bed I'm adding a roll bar arc and toolbox, glowing red tail light boxes at the rear, and a license plate using randomized pixel-art bars reading "MONSTR". Then I'm working out the windshield as a thin slanted box computed from the slope between two points to get the correct angle and length.

Calculating rotation and offset for the windshield box...

Still working out window geometry...

I'm setting the glass panels to a dark blue-gray with a diagonal highlight pattern for a subtle reflective effect, applying it to both side extrusions symmetrically. I'll skip interior details like seats since the windows are opaque, maybe just add a dark box placeholder inside the cab.

For the body paint, I'm defining a shading function with a red color ramp that lightens based on surface normal, adding flame accents on the side faces, and a racing stripe (white center, yellow edges) running along the hood, roof, and bed for faces pointing upward near the centerline.

Still shaping the flame pattern...

Still refining flame colors...

Now I'm working out the body shading with dithered ramp, deciding against fender flares given the body width, and planning the chassis details — black frame, gray axles, yellow shocks with coiled spring rings built from stacked rod geometry.

I'm adding the 4-link suspension bars connecting axles to frame, a steering link rod across the front axle, and considering how to texture the tire sidewalls with a pixel-painted pattern.

For the tire itself, I'm separating the tire body from a smaller rim disc, then stamping a tiny 3x5 pixel font onto the sidewall face to spell out something like "MEGA" as a decal.

I'm checking that the text placed at radius 0.62 near the top of the tire ring fits within the ring's inner and outer radius bounds, confirming the corners stay inside the 0.46–0.78 range. For the mirrored wheel on the opposite side, I need the decal plane to face outward in the -X direction so the text reads correctly from outside on both sides.

I also want sidewall tire detailing, like a white-lettering ring. I'm building a tire paint helper that takes a wheel's center coordinates and computes radial distance from that center for each painted cell, so I can determine whether a point falls on the end caps or sidewall ring and shade it accordingly.

Still defining paint rules...

Designing the hub disc with a pixel-based radial texture—silver lip, beadlock bolt dots, gold spokes, and a center cap—applied to a circular face geometry sized to sit flush against the tire opening.

Adding planetary hubs, a front differential sphere, and driveshaft rods connecting to the rear axle. Then placing a hood-mounted blower scoop with chrome pipes for the exposed engine detail.

Still adjusting scoop and pipe positioning...

Now I'm working out the light bar sizing and then the chassis layout—placing wheels so tires sit within the body extent, laying out frame rails and cross-members between the axles, and adding small riser blocks to mount the body to the frame.

Next I'm adding skid plates, a front bull bar with a bumper and vertical tubes, and a winch box with a yellow rope coil. Then I'm sketching out a pixel-art door decal for the number "7", planning the glyph shape and how to stamp it onto a circular badge texture.

Now I'm working out exact placement of that door roundel on the cab side, aligning it with the window bottom and body curvature, and making sure it sits on top of the flame paint job on the lower body without conflicting with it.

I'm also adding small detail elements: thin seam lines for the door edges, a door handle positioned near the back of the door, and starting to plan the mirror placement.

Moving to the rear of the model now, placing tail lights, rear bumper, and a license plate, then adding bed liner texture and rail details on top of the truck bed.

For the roll hoop, I'm building it with rounded rod segments and corner capsules rather than a single sweep, so joints look smoother. Then I'm starting to add bed contents like fuel containers.

Adding bed accessories...

For the exhaust stacks, I'm placing them just behind the cab outside the roll hoop line, using tapered rods with a slight flare near the top and a curved cap tip for realism.

Adding mud splatter patches on the lower body panels, a dark charcoal rocker/skirt band, a pixelated grille pattern of silver bars on a dark background up front, and headlight boxes sized to fit the grille width.

Still adding details...

Frame color settled, keeping flat colors for simplicity. I'm setting up helper functions for boxes and shocks, defining texel scale and wheel positioning math, then starting the main vehicle construction script with imports and builder setup.

Writing texture generators...

Picking a red/yellow flame color scheme for the truck with yellow chrome-style rims and dark spokes, plus hub shading. Now I'm sketching pixel-font glyphs for the tire sidewall lettering texture.

Placing the letter grid onto a small plane mapped to the tire face, working out the exact radial position so the text sits just outside the rim without overlapping the tire cap geometry.

I'm checking the bottom text clearance against the floor, then setting up the tire as a cylinder oriented along x with paint-based coloring. I'm also considering adding a shoulder ring near the tire edge for a chamfered sidewall look.

For the tread, I'm planning chevron-pattern lugs using two staggered rows of boxes offset and rotated slightly, but I'm wary that 24 lugs per row across four tires could push the part count toward the limit, so I need to check whether painted parts sharing a mesh count separately against that budget.

Checking the geometry, the staggered lug's lowest corner nearly touches the floor with negligible lift, so the flat bottom face sits tangent at radius 0.85, confirming solid contact at that row.

For the lug height, 0.1 spans from 0.75 to 0.85, sinking 0.03 into the tread—good positioning. I'm working out the rotation math so that a local Euler X rotation correctly maps the lug's orientation to its angular position around the tire, verifying the sine/cosine relationship holds at θ=90°-a.

Writing tire paint function...

For the mud coating, I'm blending a lowness factor from vertical position with noise and randomness to decide where mud splatters appear versus clean rubber, then distinguishing sidewall regions (dark color near the rim, a possible white stripe ring) from tread regions based on radius from center.

Still defining color ramps...

Still writing flame gradient logic...

That covers the cab lower but keeps the bed red, so no extra bed flames needed and the hood tops stay clean. I'm layering the paint order as base, then flames, stripe, mud splatter near the bottom using a randomized mud factor, then the rocker panel, and defining the glass paint pattern using UV coordinates.

Working out the glass ramp...

I'm figuring out the windshield and window shapes using trapezoid extrusions with coordinate outlines, making sure the points wind consistently, and considering whether to add a small rear window box on the cab's sloped back face.

Solving for rotation angle, I get roughly -160.4°, which I apply to the box with a slight position offset along the normal and reuse the window texture. I'm skipping fender and visor details for now and moving on to write a helper function for generating shock absorber geometry between top and bottom points.

Writing shock absorber geometry...

Working out frame rails and suspension linkage positions, placing the ladder bars connecting the axle to the frame, then sketching the triangulated 4-link geometry with upper and lower rods at slightly offset angles for each axle.

Adding the upper link geometry, then sketching underbody details: a belly skid plate, skipping fuel/battery boxes to avoid conflicts, small body-mount gap blocks between rails and body, and glow wrappers for the lights.

Now adding bumpers with bull bar tubes, a winch and tow hooks up front, plus a rear bumper with a license plate decal.

Rear tail lights sit as small boxes flanking the bumper, with a pixelated license plate texture drawn procedurally in yellow with dark border and random glyph-like bars. Then I'm moving to the hood, adding a scoop with a blower box.

Still adding scoop details...

Placing lamps across the light bar with a warm glow and dark reflectors behind, deciding to skip the antenna and sun-strip details for simplicity, then starting on the bed liner with a ribbed texture positioned at the rear.

Adding a roll hoop behind the bed using angled capsule struts with a chrome finish, plus amber light pods mounted on top. I'm also positioning dual exhaust stacks outside the body edge, checking their placement against the rear tire bounds so they don't clip.

Now I'm adding stack brackets, side mirrors, fender flares at the front bumper corners, and running boards along the body sides.

I'm also positioning mud flaps behind the front and rear tires as small boxes hanging from the body bottom, checking their placement relative to tire z-extents and bumper locations so they don't clip.

I'll skip the splash guards and keep the tires hanging outside the body like a real monster truck. For the windshield wipers, I'm adding thin dark rods positioned diagonally across the windshield glass, calculating endpoints along the glass plane with a slight normal offset so they sit just above the surface.

Working out the second wiper rod positioned parallel to the first, offset slightly in x, with thin dark rods for both. Then checking the glass box dimensions and center position to confirm it stays within the body's width bounds.

I'm sketching a few extra details: a small visor box above the windshield, door and grille lines, a roundel sign, and a "TURBO" decal spelled out using a pixel glyph font for each letter.

I'm writing a reusable text-texture generator that builds letters as pixel grids with an optional outline, sized based on string length, then placing this "TURBO" decal on the bed's side panel using the body's existing coordinate system.

Still writing glyph rendering logic...

Now thinking through the dressing details—a fuel can in olive-green with a spout, skipping the tow chain, and underside elements like the front diff. For bumper brackets and bolts, I'm considering merging small box geometries with BufferGeometryUtils to keep the part count manageable, maybe around 60 bolts total.

I'm estimating total part counts: roughly 240 across all four tires (treads, rims, discs, caps, nuts, text), plus about 120 for the body, keeping things under 700 to stay safely below the 1000-part limit. I'm trimming lug nut counts to 5 per wheel with 20 lugs per row at 18° spacing, giving 40 lugs per wheel and 160 total, with beadlock bolts baked into the texture instead of modeled geometry. Now I'm positioning cylindrical lug nuts around each wheel's radius.

Defining rim geometry...

Building cylinder and glow helpers, then setting up the body extrusion with a typed outline array for the shape points.

Skipping the underbody strip and arch decoration for now since the body bottom sits above the tires fine. For the grille, I'm checking the slanted front face geometry against the box dimensions - the position and size line up closely enough, with just a small mismatch I could fix by rotating the box slightly to match the slope instead.

For the headlights, I'm placing chrome-bezeled boxes matching the grille's rotation and angle, with warm glow coloring, and considering a small pixel texture for the lens with a ring highlight to give it more detail.

I'll skip turn signals for simplicity. Settling on a color palette (steel, chrome, dark frame, yellow, blue) and axle positions (±1.7 z), then moving to writing the full file with axle housings and hidden brake discs.

Adding differential cover with bolt details...

Placing bolt rings on the diff cover and setting the housing color, then working out shock mount positions — top brackets near the rail ends and bottom brackets on the axle, checking clearances against tire width.

I'll do four shocks total, one per side per axle, plus a front tie-rod for steering and skip the valve stem detail. Now starting the final code assembly, importing the builder utilities and paint helpers.

Setting up imports and types...

Simplifying the mud function to depend only on the z-coordinate, combining radial distance, height falloff, and noise to decide where mud splatters appear on the tire, while avoiding the sidewall text region.

For the rubber coloring I'm defining sidewall rings (dark edge, white stripe) based on radius, and treads use a gradient pick of rubber shades. I'm finalizing this as version v02, applying the same paint function to lug parts using axis-based normals, and noting the lug rotation formula before writing everything to file.
